principles: No cookies. No local storage. No advertising identifiers. No cross-site tracking.
No personal data is collected: no name, no email, no IP address, no user agent, no device fingerprint.
A search is recorded as a length and a result count, never as the words the reader typed.
Every event carries a random per-page-load session id that is discarded when the tab closes, so sessions can be counted but not profiled.
The collector is first-party and self-hosted. If no collector is deployed, the script is inert and the site works normally.
Amazon-side conversions are never measured here. Orders and commission appear only in the campaign ledger, and only when transcribed from an authorised Associates report.

endpoint.content_type: application/json on fetch, text/plain on sendBeacon
endpoint.health_probe: GET /api/collect returns 200 {"status":"ok"}. The browser client sends this once per page load and only switches measurement on when it succeeds, so a site with no collector deployed behaves exactly like a site with no analytics at all.

implementations.note: A GET on the same path answers the health probe, so one route serves both the probe and the event sink.

implementations.storage: newline-delimited JSON appended to a local file
implementations.note: Dependency-free, no npm install, no build step. Run it on any host and point the site at it with <meta name="x-collect-endpoint" content="https://host/collect">.

endpoint.failure_behaviour: A failed or unreachable collector is swallowed silently. It never blocks navigation and never produces a console error in a reader's browser.
what_is_never_stored: Device fingerprint or any derived identifier
The full referrer URL (only the bare hostname is kept, and only when it is a different host)
The text of a search query
Any key outside the documented event schema

events.name: page_view
events.title: A page of the publication was viewed
events.fires: On every full page load of a page on this site.
events.why_it_exists: The denominator. Every other number is meaningless without it.

events.name: outbound_click
events.title: A reader clicked a sponsored outbound link to Amazon
events.fires: On click of any anchor carrying a data-outbound product id, immediately before navigation.
events.why_it_exists: The only first-party number that measures intent to buy. It is the top of the funnel that the Associates report eventually completes.
not_collected: the destination URL of the click

events.name: guide_read
events.title: A guide was actually read
events.fires: When the footer of a guide scrolls into view, which means the reader reached the end of it.
events.why_it_exists: Distinguishes a guide that was opened from a guide that was read. It is the closest proxy this site has to engagement, and it is the number that should decide which topics get more coverage.

events.name: search
events.title: A reader searched the site
events.fires: On a search results page that has a query.

payload.query_length: string, the number of characters typed
payload.result_count: string, the number of results shown

events.why_it_exists: Shows what readers cannot find by browsing, which is the cheapest editorial signal available. It names a topic; it never repeats the words a reader typed.

events.name: suggestion_rank
events.title: A reader reordered the suggestions register
events.fires: When a reader moves a suggestion up or down in the rank table.
events.why_it_exists: The suggestions register is a decision surface. This shows which directions readers think should be built first, without asking them to fill in a form.

not_measured_here.where_it_comes_from: The Associates Central orders report, transcribed into the campaign ledger by hand, with the report date and a link to the report recorded.
The same first-party report. It is never estimated.
Orders divided by clicks, and only once both sides are real. No proxy conversion rate is published.

status.endpoint: shipped in repository, not deployed to a public host
status.why_not_deployed: GitHub Pages serves static files only and cannot run a server-side function. The endpoint ships in two deployable forms so the site owner can run it wherever they like. Until one is deployed and pointed at, the collector stays inert and the campaign ledger stays empty.
